chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Dance's afterword: Mildred's last phone call
summary: Dance adds that Red stayed close to Mildred and her last call that night was to him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well -- JR the one thing -- Red has gone, and I remember the one thing I did want to get down on tape, which I forgot to ask him about or which I think you probably know, but it's worth mentioning, I think, and that was further to his relationship with Mildred, they remained close friends, I guess from probably about -- must've been about seven years, because I think the children were six and three or something, and Red used to take the children when he'd come to New York, he'd take the children up to the farm where Mildred was. She was so crazy about the children, I even think that Eve went up, too, anyway it was a very nice relationship. And Mildred was crazy about those children.

And, so their relationship just remained close, she and Red, and whenever she had problems, which naturally she was getting more sick, she had problems, she'd always turn to Red, and matter of course he'd see the lawyer for her, talk to her accountant, do whatever was necessary, also with Eve's blessing. And so when -- you know when she died, that very day, that she was up in hospital in Poughkeepsie or somewhere and she called him about 8:00 o'clock at night, she was talking to him and he told her what the lawyer had said and so on, and he went to work, I think he was at -- at

Michael's Pub or the Embers or somewhere and he went to work and he said, then about 10:30 or something there was an urgent phone call which he took and it was from Eve she said the hospital just called him. To say that Mildred had died in her sleep and he was the last person that she ever talked to.

Which was very fitting, and very appropriate, I think, and very moving. I should think it's a most unusual sequel to a marriage and I just thought that that should be down in this, so I tell you it and maybe you can include it as a footnote or something. Okay. Thanks.
